name: Learned dynamics
summary: Replace part of the explicit simulator with a learned component while keeping the rest differentiable. The first concrete step toward structured generative worlds.

tasks.title: Learn a residual correction to the grid update
tasks.note: Keep the MLS-MPM step but add a small learned residual on the grid velocity, trained through the differentiable rollout. A minimal hybrid that tests whether gradients can train a network embedded in physics.

tasks.title: Learned residual against a hard mismatch (non-smooth / nonlinear / stronger held-out)
tasks.note: learned-residual closed ~100% (train) and 66.7% (held-out v0) of a LINEAR drag gap — the friendliest possible mismatch (smooth, near-linear, velocity-only). The bounded 0.1*tanh residual was adequate only because the missing physics was weak. Natural follow-up the task flagged as open: a genuinely hard mismatch — a non-smooth contact law, anisotropic / state-dependent drag, or perturbed gravity — and a stronger held-out shift (blob shape, resolution, mismatch type), not just a new v0. This separates 'a promising demonstration' from 'a method': does the late-residual trainability survive when the target is non-smooth and the residual must be larger (re-risking the blow-up the bound prevents)?
